messages:
jia: Running into a confusing Python SDK issue: async client + function-calling + structured_output. Tool results arrive as a JSON-encoded string instead of a dict, which breaks TypedDict consumers.

tomas: can you paste a tiny repro?

jia: sure:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key='...')
resp = await client.chat.create(
  model='gpt-xyz',
  messages=[{'role':'user','content':'invoke user_lookup(9) and return JSON'}],
  tools=[{'name':'user_lookup','schema':{'id':int,'email':str}}],
)
# resp.choices[0].message.tool_result -> '\"{\\"id\\":9,\\"email\\":\\"a@b.com\\"}\"'  # string, not dict
```

ana: interesting — sync client returns parsed dict?

jia: yes sync is fine. Async path seems to either double-encode the payload or skip parsing after streaming. SDK 0.9.3.

ci-bot: nightly tests flagged py/test_tools_async.py::test_tool_result_types (RDW-540).

tomas: likely the async streaming deserializer isn't calling json.loads on the assembled chunks when structured_output schema is present. Two fixes: buffer+parse in async adapter, and tighten return typing on AsyncClient.chat.create to TypedDict|str.

ana: short-term workaround: helper func parse_tool(x) -> dict that does json.loads if isinstance(x,str) else x. Update quickstart to show that.

jia: will add repro and logs to the ticket. Also please include a mypy test so the typing change is enforced.

docs-team: noted, we'll mark async tool sample with a caveat and include helper snippet.

tomas: assigning RDW-540 to me. I'll add failing test, implement buffer+parse, and update typing stubs. PR soon.

ci-bot: RDW-540 created and assigned to tomas. PR draft expected this sprint.
